findings.title: Account the full final SSH and remote handoff interval
findings.detail: The client books elapsed+5 seconds and times out its own SSH after5 seconds. The remote bootstrap starts a separate5-second monotonic window only after the SSH command arrives. Killing/timing out local SSH does not prove termination of the remote bootstrap. With4 seconds of connection/delivery delay and4 seconds of remote bootstrap work, the dispatcher can start8 seconds after the client invocation while only5 seconds is charged. run_science then starts a new monotonic origin; its additional science-handoff reservation does not cover that omitted transport/bootstrap interval. This can undercharge the300s preflight phase and shift the3120s cumulative deadline.
findings.required_change: Use an enforceable end-to-end final dispatch envelope or explicitly charge separate bounded connection and remote bootstrap envelopes, entirely inside the unchanged300s. Keep unknown outcomes no-retry. Add a pure synthetic delayed-delivery/client-timeout case that proves no uncharged remote launch is admitted; update plan/prose consistently.

findings.title: Admit the combined remote upload size before SCP
findings.detail: The pretransport check verifies only local_archive_roots<=fixed_local_archive_bytes. It never checks fixed_local_archive_bytes+payload_bytes plus initial remote metadata allowance against the single1GiB cap. bootstrap-create checks an almost-empty remote root; SCP can then create the entire payload.tar without a remote watcher. If the manifest parameters leave insufficient combined capacity, the first combined-size rejection is after the full over-cap tar has already been uploaded. Final payload bytes are not yet frozen, so this review cannot establish that the assembled package avoids the path.
findings.required_change: Before any transport, reject unless the frozen local charge plus the full planned remote wire bytes and bounded bootstrap/control overhead fit the one1GiB cap. Bind/check this admission in the final action manifest; do not rely on a post-upload guard. Add a pure fixture proving over-cap payloads never invoke SSH/SCP.
